terms.definition: Application Programming Interface — a set of rules and protocols that allows one software application to communicate with another
terms.example: When your banking app shows your balance, it called a GET API. When you transfer money, it called a POST API

terms.definition: Representational State Transfer API — a design style using HTTP methods on resource-based URLs. The most popular API style worldwide
terms.example: GET /orders retrieves orders. POST /orders creates one. The URL is the noun; the method is the verb

terms.definition: A verb that indicates what action to perform on a resource: GET (read), POST (create), PUT (update/replace), DELETE (remove), PATCH (partial update)
terms.example: GET /users/42 reads user 42. DELETE /users/42 removes them. Same URL, different actions

terms.definition: A specific URL where an API resource can be accessed. Combines the base URL, stage, and resource path
terms.example: https://abc123.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/prod/orders is a full endpoint

terms.definition: Create, Read, Update, Delete — the four basic operations on data. Maps to POST (Create), GET (Read), PUT (Update), DELETE (Delete)
terms.example: A todo app uses all four: create a task (POST), view tasks (GET), mark complete (PUT), remove task (DELETE)

terms.definition: AWS's fully managed service that acts as the front door for backend services — handling routing, authentication, throttling, caching, and monitoring
terms.example: Like a reception desk: it receives all requests, checks who's allowed, routes them to the right specialist, and returns the response

terms.definition: A URL path in API Gateway representing a logical entity. Resources form a tree from root /
terms.example: /orders is a resource for the orders collection. /orders/{orderId} is a resource for a specific order

terms.definition: An HTTP verb (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) attached to a resource in API Gateway, defining what actions clients can perform
terms.example: GET /orders returns the order list. POST /orders creates a new order. Both are methods on the /orders resource

terms.definition: The backend service API Gateway forwards requests to. Options: Lambda function, HTTP endpoint, AWS service directly, or Mock
terms.example: A GET /orders method integration points to the orders-handler Lambda function

terms.definition: An integration setting where API Gateway passes the full HTTP request as a JSON event to Lambda, and Lambda returns an object with statusCode, headers, and body
terms.example: The event object includes httpMethod, path, headers, queryStringParameters, and body — Lambda reads all of this

terms.definition: A named reference to a deployment of your API representing an environment (dev, staging, prod), each with its own invoke URL and configuration
terms.example: The dev stage URL: https://abc.execute-api.region.amazonaws.com/dev/orders. The prod URL uses /prod instead

terms.definition: A key-value configuration pair at the stage level, commonly used to point each stage to a different Lambda alias or function version
terms.example: Stage variable lambdaAlias=prod in prod stage, lambdaAlias=dev in dev stage — same API routes to different Lambda code

terms.definition: An explicit action in API Gateway that publishes the current state of your API (resources, methods, integrations) to a stage, making changes live
terms.example: After adding a new /payments resource, you must click Deploy API → prod stage for clients to be able to call it

terms.definition: AWS's serverless compute service — runs your code in response to events without any server management. You pay per millisecond of execution
terms.example: An orders Lambda function runs when API Gateway triggers it, queries DynamoDB, and returns the result — no server needed

terms.definition: An IAM role attached to a Lambda function that grants it permissions to access other AWS services like DynamoDB, S3, or CloudWatch
terms.example: An orders Lambda needs dynamodb:PutItem permission in its execution role to write orders to DynamoDB

terms.definition: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing — HTTP headers that tell browsers it's safe to allow JavaScript requests from a different domain than the server
terms.example: Frontend at myshop.com calling API at execute-api.amazonaws.com — without CORS headers, the browser blocks the request

terms.definition: A browser security rule that blocks JavaScript from making requests to a different domain than the page's own domain. CORS is the mechanism to relax this
terms.example: JavaScript at myshop.com can call myshop.com/api freely, but needs CORS headers to call amazonaws.com/api

terms.definition: An HTTP method automatically created by API Gateway when you enable CORS. Browsers send an OPTIONS preflight request before cross-origin POST/PUT calls
terms.example: Before your browser sends a POST to the API, it first sends OPTIONS to check if the API allows cross-origin requests from your domain

terms.definition: An alphanumeric string generated in API Gateway and distributed to clients, who include it in requests via the x-api-key header. Used with Usage Plans for per-client access control
terms.example: Partner A gets key ABC123 associated with a 1,000/day plan. Partner B gets key XYZ789 associated with a 10,000/day plan

terms.definition: A configuration in API Gateway that sets throttle (rate/burst) and quota (daily/weekly/monthly) limits for an API key, enabling per-client rate limiting
terms.example: basic-plan: 10 RPS, burst 5, 1,000 requests/day. premium-plan: 100 RPS, burst 50, 100,000 requests/day

terms.definition: A Lambda function that API Gateway calls before the backend to validate a token and return an IAM policy (allow or deny). Used for custom authentication logic
terms.example: A Lambda Authorizer checks a proprietary token against your auth database and returns allow if valid, deny if expired

terms.definition: An API Gateway authorizer that validates JWT tokens from Amazon Cognito User Pools, providing managed user authentication without custom code
terms.example: A mobile app user logs in via Cognito, gets a JWT, includes it in API calls. API Gateway validates the JWT automatically

terms.definition: API Gateway's mechanism to limit request rates to protect backend services from being overwhelmed. Returns 429 Too Many Requests when exceeded
terms.example: Default limits: 10,000 RPS steady, 5,000 burst. Exceeding either returns 429 to the caller
